exposure: Time points: 3 days old and 30-42 days old
outcome: Abundance of specific bacterial genera (Bifidobacterium, Lactobacillus, Escherichia-Shigella, Bacteroides, Staphylococcus, Streptococcus, Corynebacterium)
finding: Vaginally delivered infants had a higher abundance of beneficial gut bacteria, such as Bifidobacterium and Lactobacillus, and a different gut microbiota composition and predicted function compared to cesarean-delivered infants at both 3 days and 30-42 days of age.
mod_finding: Infants born via cesarean section had a lower abundance of Bifidobacterium and Lactobacillus, and a higher abundance of Staphylococcus and Streptococcus, compared to vaginally born infants at both time points.
